deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is the closing formula of a letter: 'und Bewunderung zu beharren als / Ew. Hochwohlgeboren / [long bracket] / ewig(?) dankbarer Schüler / B. Riemann', with place and date at left: 'Göttingen, den 12. Juni 1850.' It completes the sentence begun on the previous page: 'Gestatten Sie mir, unter der Versicherung der höchsten Verehrung und Bewunderung zu beharren als Ew. Hochwohlgeboren ... dankbarer Schüler B. Riemann.' The faint mirrored lines visible across the page are bleed-through from the other side of the leaf, i.e. the previous page's text about the equations k, k', ..., omega, dx'/dx, and so on. They are not new content.

Context. The next sheet is an envelope or wrapper addressed to Heinrich Weber: 'Brief von Riemann an Gauss nebst Erläuterungen von Mayer', given by Schering on 27.11.1894 for possible use in a third edition of the Werke. So the letter is from the 23-year-old Riemann to Gauss. 'G. g. A.' on the previous page means the Göttingische gelehrte Anzeigen, where Gauss's 1815 review of Pfaff's 'Methodus generalis' appeared. The letter comments on the conditions under which Pfaff's reduction (transformation) of a Pfaffian equation is carried out. Riemann distinguishes requiring δt ≠ 0 from requiring δx ≠ 0. He also treats the degenerate case where some of the equations depend on the others, and remarks that the transformation is then possible for both even and odd n.

No derivation appears on this page itself.

results.what: Closing and signature of a letter from Riemann to Gauss (Göttingen, 12 June 1850) on the conditions in Pfaff's method for Pfaffian equations, as described in Gauss's GGA review
results.modern_name: Pfaff problem (reduction of a Pfaffian form to normal form); this page has only the letter's closing
results.usually_credited_to: J. F. Pfaff (1815); Gauss's review in the GGA (1815); later Jacobi, Frobenius, Darboux

deep.surprise_reason: The page is only the valediction, date and signature of a letter. It has no mathematical content. The letter's existence is documented by the Weber/Schering annotation on the next page.
transcription_corrections: The word before 'dankbarer Schüler' is most plausibly 'ewig' ('ewig dankbarer Schüler'), not 'ganz'.
The opening line reads 'und Bewunderung zu beharren als', which continues '...unter der Versicherung der höchsten Verehrung' from the previous page.
The large curved bracket between 'Ew. Hochwohlgeboren' and the signature is a calligraphic letter-closing device, not text.
The faint mirrored writing across the page is show-through from the reverse side, not additional content.
